newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares end off their bottom levels on Monday as Wall Street opens firmer, but local stocks still finish much weaker after their earlier hit by the Dow's nearly 250 point plunge on Friday, dealers said.
They said the local market remained very nervous, warily watching to see how Wall Street trade pans out and anxious its firmer open may not hold.

"The market kicked up a little off its bottom with the Dow starting up, but the local market is very, very nervous and not responding as positively as might have been hoped," said David Shapiro of Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
"The market is taking a few steps backwards to see how Wall Street pans out -- whether there will be an aftershock or whether it can hold its gains," Shapiro added.

Dealers said that the day's thin volumes indicate that players have not been panicked into selling. Removing overnight trades, only 500 million rands worth of shares traded on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Monday, they said.
"Although performance is down, it's encouraging that volumes are particularly low," a trader said.
Of the 478 shares traded, there were 327 declining, 75 advancing and 76 unchanged.
South African and world markets alike were awaiting U.S. Federal Reserve Bank Governor Alan Greenspan's address on Tuesday for news on U.S. interest rates which was seen offering Wall St direction.
Any recovery in U.S. stocks was seen buoying local shares but shares were seen treading carefully for a while.
"Greenspan could bring some comfort to that market and there could be some recovery but we're in a very sensitive time right now," Shapiro said.
Industrial shares finished 71.9 points down at 9,049.0 points, all-shares lost 78.5 points to 7,361.3 points and gold shares dipped 5.8 points to 1,016.4 points.
Shares were whacked at the start by Wall Street's Friday plunge with industrial index opening down 103.4 points, then sinking further before slowly recovering ground.
Some futures-related buying helped push shares up in early afternoon and dealers said there were a number of bargain hunters around.
Gold shares enjoyed some small interest after falling in sympathy with the overall market with some dealers saying a pull-back from equities could boost bullion.

Small shares were the biggest traders by volume but dealers said some demand was seen for blue chips with De Beers trading 525,200 shares -- although a large slice of that was overnight trade from Friday.
De Beers closed 275 cents down at 147.25 rand.
Sasol also enjoyed big trade with 563,700 shares changing hands. That share closed steady at 59.50 rand.
Wall Street's plunge also pulled South African share futures contracts back, dealers said.
But, in line with market expectations, those contracts did not slide much further on the day.
Near-term all-share contracts were last at 6,432/43 from 6,570, industrials were at 8,440/45 from 8,569 and golds at 730/45 from 747.
